title: Ledger Expands Crypto Wallet Tampering Probe to Berlin and Dubai
summary: Physically altered Ledger wallets surfaced beyond Southeast Asia in the same incident the company disclosed in October. Ledger is offering factory inspections after finding that the modifications were designed to capture wallet recovery phrases during setup. Ledger Finds Tampered Wallets in Berlin L...
content:
Physically altered Ledger wallets surfaced beyond Southeast Asia in the same incident the company disclosed in October. Ledger is offering factory inspections after finding that the modifications were designed to capture wallet recovery phrases during setup.

Key Takeaways

  • Ledger is investigating two reports of wallet tampering in Dubai.
  • One affected Nano Gen 5 wallet surfaced in Southeast Asia.
  • Berlin buyers concerned about third-party purchases since January should contact Ledger Support.

Ledger Finds Tampered Wallets in Berlin

Ledger said Nov. 18 that it had found tampered crypto wallets in Berlin and was investigating two reports in Dubai. The hardware wallet investigation update said every confirmed device showed the same kind of physical modification. The company added:

“There is no flaw in Ledger’s secure chip or operating system, and no confirmed case involving a device bought on ledger.com.”

In a publicly reported Dubai case, a tracker run by former Mt. Gox CEO Mark Karpeles lists a confirmed implant in a Ledger Flex reportedly purchased in Dubai. Ledger said it was working with distribution partners to trace how the devices in the Dubai reports entered circulation.

The company described the total number of affected devices as small and said it expected to find more. Its security team is examining suspected devices, while Ledger reviews distribution records with its partners and works with law enforcement.

Retailers Paused Sales in Germany and Asia

A German customer’s report of a suspected implant had already prompted the October MediaMarktSaturn sales suspension in stores and online. Ledger said at the time that the customer had reported no loss of funds.

The October sales pause across seven Asian markets covered authorized sellers in six Southeast Asian markets and Hong Kong. Ledger said genuine devices were altered before reaching buyers. The regional probe remains active, and the company has identified one affected Ledger Nano Gen 5.

CryptoBilis, a Southeast Asian reseller named in the Ledger probe, changed ownership in March, according to founder Arravind Prabu.

Trezor’s Safe 5 investigation found implants in three devices sold by CryptoBilis. Trezor said Nov. 12 that it had cut its reseller network by about 80% and released a firmware update to block the implants it identified.

What Ledger Advises Buyers to Do

Ledger advised concerned customers who bought from third-party sellers in Southeast Asia, Berlin, or Dubai to contact its support team. The Berlin advisory covers purchases from January 2026 onward. For a limited time, Ledger Support can arrange physical inspections, including X-rays, at the company’s factory in Vierzon, France.

Ledger says customers who suspect tampering should stop using the device and not use it to set up or restore a wallet. It advises moving funds to a new wallet using a fresh recovery phrase generated on a device bought directly from Ledger. The phrase created when setting up a hardware wallet can restore access to funds on another device.

The company advises against reusing the old recovery phrase or passphrase and recommends reporting suspected tampering to local authorities. Ledger Support will never ask for a customer’s 24-word recovery phrase.

title: Bitcoin Advocacy Group Sets Sights on Washington’s Open-Source AI Debate
summary: The Bitcoin Policy Institute (BPI) is rebranding as the Finney Foundation for Open Technology, expanding its policy advocacy beyond bitcoin to include open-source artificial intelligence (AI) and other technologies. Bringing Bitcoin’s Advocacy Model to Open-Source AI The Bitcoin Policy Institute (BP...
content:
The Bitcoin Policy Institute (BPI) is rebranding as the Finney Foundation for Open Technology, expanding its policy advocacy beyond bitcoin to include open-source artificial intelligence (AI) and other technologies.

Key Takeaways

  • BPI’s 2026 rebrand expands its policy agenda to open-source AI, digital cash, and emerging technologies.
  • Jack Dorsey highlighted open-source AI at BPI’s September summit, warning against control by one company or government.
  • Finney Foundation’s 2026 launch introduces research fellows to advance open technology and individual liberty.

Bringing Bitcoin’s Advocacy Model to Open-Source AI

The Bitcoin Policy Institute (BPI), a nonpartisan think tank focused on shaping Washington’s approach to cryptocurrency policy, is rebranding as the Finney Foundation for Open Technology. The rebranded entity also said it is expanding its advocacy agenda to include open-source artificial intelligence (AI), digital cash and other emerging technologies.

Despite the broader policy mandate, the foundation’s leadership maintains that bitcoin will remain a cornerstone of its work. As U.S. lawmakers and federal agencies grapple with developing regulatory frameworks for AI, the foundation said in a statement that it intends to replicate the advocacy model it developed for bitcoin. Its strategy centers on persuading policymakers and educating the public that open systems outperform closed alternatives, and that American technological leadership is best achieved through openness.

The urgency of this shift was a central theme at BPI’s Freedom Tech DC summit in September. Highlighting the growing convergence of these technologies, Block co-founder Jack Dorsey told attendees:

“The next and probably largest element [of freedom technology] is open intelligence and making sure that it’s not locked up in the hands of any one government or any one company… that’s where we’re going to get the best outcomes.”

David Zell, president of the Finney Foundation, pointed to the think tank’s growing influence in Washington since its inception as evidence of the effectiveness of its advocacy model.

“We set out to make Washington think about Bitcoin differently—to educate them on the importance of open monetary networks,” Zell said in a statement. “Our fellows now serve in congressional offices for both parties and in the executive branch. Our ideas have shaped discourse and policy. Our expansion will help us stay at the forefront of today’s most consequential policy debates, especially those around open-source AI.”

Foundation Unveils Open Technology Declaration and Research Fellows

To mark its public launch, the foundation unveiled its Open Technology Declaration, which advances the principle that machines should serve humanity rather than exercise control over it.

The organization also introduced its inaugural class of Finney Fellows, a multidisciplinary group of researchers specializing in machine intelligence, free speech, national security, biotechnology, and space exploration.

By bringing these fields under a unified open-technology agenda, the Finney Foundation aims to influence policies that ensure the next wave of technological innovation strengthens individual liberty rather than concentrating power in the hands of governments or corporations.

title: Anthropic Sets $83 IPO Price After Crypto Traders Bet Near $98
summary: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share and increased the offering to 980 million shares, putting gross proceeds at $81.34 billion before fees. A pre-IPO contract tied to Anthropic stock traded near $98 on Nov. 18 ahead of the company’s expected Nasdaq debut. Anthropic’s $83 IPO Price Sets a Benchma...
content:
Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share and increased the offering to 980 million shares, putting gross proceeds at $81.34 billion before fees. A pre-IPO contract tied to Anthropic stock traded near $98 on Nov. 18 ahead of the company’s expected Nasdaq debut.

Key Takeaways

  • Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share, above its $70 to $78 range.
  • A pre-IPO contract tied to Anthropic traded about 18% above the $83 offer price.
  • Pre-IPO contracts correctly signaled whether shares would open above or below their offer price in seven of eight IPOs Grayscale reviewed.

Anthropic’s $83 IPO Price Sets a Benchmark for Crypto Bets

Anthropic priced its initial public offering at $83 a share on Nov. 18, above its preliminary range of $70 to $78. The Trade.xyz contract on Hyperliquid traded near $98 at 4:35 p.m. EST that day, about $15 above the offer price. The company’s Nasdaq debut, expected Nov. 19 under the symbol ANT, will show whether its first public trade clears the $83 offer price.

In a Nov. 18 analysis of pre-IPO trading, Grayscale head of research Zach Pandl and senior research associate Michael Zhao cited a Trade.xyz contract price near $96. Their comparison used the $78 top of the preliminary range as the benchmark.

Pandl and Zhao wrote:

“If they are right, Anthropic’s shares could open roughly 23% above the company’s filed range.”

Using Hyperliquid data, Grayscale found that pre-IPO contracts correctly signaled whether shares would open above or below their offer prices in seven of eight listings from May through October. The review covered Cerebras, Quantinuum, SpaceX, SK Hynix’s American depositary receipt (ADR), CXMT, Unitree, Shein’s Hong Kong listing, and Jio.

Shein was the sole exception. Its contract pointed to an opening about 9% below the offer price, but shares opened at the offer price and fell 10% within the first hour. Grayscale’s review measured whether the opening was above or below the offer price, so a correct call could still leave a gap between the contract price and the opening trade.

Trade.xyz’s ANT-USDC contract on Hyperliquid traded near $98 at 4:35 p.m. EST on Nov. 18.

Anthropic Expanded the IPO to 980 Million Shares

Anthropic’s Nov. 17 amended registration statement proposed a sale of 825 million Class A shares. The final deal added 155 million shares, all from Anthropic. The company will sell about 956.4 million shares, and existing stockholders will sell about 23.6 million.

At the high end of the preliminary range, the 825 million shares Anthropic marketed during its IPO roadshow would have generated $64.35 billion before fees and expenses. The higher price and larger share count added $16.99 billion to that figure. About $79.38 billion of the final offering’s gross proceeds would go to Anthropic, with the balance going to selling stockholders.

The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission declared the registration statement effective on Nov. 18. Anthropic expects the offering to close Nov. 20, subject to customary closing conditions. Underwriters have a 30-day option to buy up to 147 million more shares, which are outside the $81.34 billion base offering.

How Anthropic’s Pre-IPO Contracts Work

The Trade.xyz instrument is a cash-settled pre-IPO perpetual, a type of derivative contract without a fixed expiration date. Traders can take positions on where they expect the stock to trade, with gains and losses settled in cash. The contract conveys no ownership in Anthropic, so a position carries no shareholder rights.

Before a public stock price exists, each provider sets its own method for establishing a reference price. Grayscale described Trade.xyz as setting a starting price and then letting traders determine where the contract moves. Entropy, another provider on Hyperliquid, combines its own trading data with private-market prices. Both contracts switch to tracking Nasdaq prices after the listing, Grayscale said.

Crypto traders had already taken positions linked to Anthropic on other venues by September. Those markets used their own contract terms and share-count assumptions to estimate a company valuation before Anthropic publicly filed for its IPO in October.

In June, Defillama began tracking pre-IPO contracts tied to Anthropic, OpenAI, SpaceX, and Quantinuum. The data aggregator tracked three Anthropic markets among 14 hosted on platforms including Aster, Lighter, and ApeX.

Multiple stock tokenization platforms also plan to offer Anthropic exposure on Thursday once trading begins, including Ondo Finance and xStocks.

title: Trump administration unveils new center to choke off scam payments
summary: Americans reported more than $17.7 billion in online fraud losses in 2025.
content:
The Trump administration has unveiled a new Threat Disruption Center, aimed at stopping money flows to foreign criminal networks behind scams, cybercrime and sextortion schemes.

The Homeland Security Task Force’s National Coordination Center, co-led by the departments of Homeland Security and Justice, announced the launch of the unit on Wednesday. It seeks to help more than 30 federal agencies and over 440 state and local partners track scams and work with banks and crypto platforms to stop payments to scam networks.

The Homeland Security statement said the center was created under a March 2026 executive order that directed federal agencies to work with private companies to combat online fraud and other cybercrime targeting Americans.

“Every hour between a victim’s report and a response gives criminals more time to launder stolen funds and identify their next target,” said Heith Janke, operations director of the FBI’s Criminal Branch.

Blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs said it was selected as the center’s main private-sector partner, according to a statement Wednesday. TRM Labs will provide Ardence, the investigative platform the center will use to map scam networks and identify victims.

“These scammers rarely stop after one payment — they drain a victim’s savings, or their retirement, over months and years,” said Esteban Castano, co-founder and CEO of TRM Labs.

“Stepping in sooner changes everything: a warning before the next payment, a scam website removed before it victimizes another family, or stolen funds frozen while they can still be recovered.

The FBI received about 453,000 reports of online fraud in 2025, with reported losses exceeding $17.7 billion.

In September, the Justice Department estimated that overseas scam centers cost Americans about $10 billion a year through schemes including crypto and online investment fraud.

title: Fed officials saw October rate hold as a ‘close call,’ minutes show
summary: The latest FOMC minutes suggest greater appetite for higher rates than the Fed’s 10–2 vote indicated, with markets now pricing in a December hike.
content:
While the Federal Open Market Committee decided not to raise interest rates during its October meeting, some participants who supported holding rates steady considered the decision a “close call,” according to newly released minutes Wednesday.

The Federal Open Market Committee voted 10–2 in October to keep its benchmark rate at 3.75% to 4%. Fed Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack favored a quarter-point increase.

“The minutes suggest broader support for an October hike than the 10–2 vote alone implied — and that was before payrolls and CPI both came in hot,” Lewis Huang, an analyst at crypto exchange Bitget, told Cointelegraph.

Markets are now overwhelmingly expecting a December rate hike. CME FedWatch has put the odds of a December quarter-point hike at about 90% and a half-point increase at about 10% at the time of writing.

“With a December hike already fully priced in, the focus shifts to the size of the move and the policy path beyond December,” said Huang.

“Governor Waller has said a half-point increase should be considered; evidence that other officials were already open to that scale of tightening in October could push the odds of a 50-basis-point move higher,” he added.

Fed officials flag AI concerns

Fed officials also raised concerns about ongoing inflationary pressures due to the AI build-out, with participants noting the demand for AI technology was pushing up the price of some consumer goods.

Related: Hot US inflation raises odds of half-point Fed hike in December

Officials separately discussed the financial risks if the returns on AI investments failed to live up to investor expectations.

“Most participants observed that AI-related debt had grown rapidly and that much of this growth had taken place through complex and opaque financing structures,” the minutes show. “A few participants remarked that AI-related exposures were becoming increasingly concentrated among a small number of firms.”

Fabian Dori, chief investment officer at Sygnum Bank, said markets are already pricing in a series of hikes into next year.

“That likely keeps long-term yields and the dollar firm, and the question for Bitcoin is whether debasement concerns and advancing institutional adoption can outweigh it,” Dori said.

title: DBS and Circle Bring 24/7 USDC Settlement to Institutions in Asia
summary: Eligible institutions will gain a direct way to switch between U.S. dollars and USDC through DBS at any hour. The service adds a cash management option for treasury teams working across time zones. USDC Gets a Direct Issuance and Redemption Route Through DBS Eligible institutional clients in Asia wi...
content:
Eligible institutions will gain a direct way to switch between U.S. dollars and USDC through DBS at any hour. The service adds a cash management option for treasury teams working across time zones.

Key Takeaways

  • Eligible clients will have a direct route to USDC through DBS.
  • The planned service offers near-instant settlement for dollar and USDC conversions.
  • In a DBS survey, 88% of large companies were using or testing tokenized money.

USDC Gets a Direct Issuance and Redemption Route Through DBS

Eligible institutional clients in Asia will be able to obtain newly issued USDC and redeem it for U.S. dollars directly through DBS, under a partnership announced in Singapore on Nov. 18 by the bank and Circle Internet Group Inc. (NYSE: CRCL). The bank channel would give clients an alternative to trading USDC on secondary markets. The companies gave no start date.

USDC is a dollar-backed stablecoin that Circle issues through regulated affiliates and was designed to track the value of the U.S. dollar. When clients mint USDC, they exchange dollars for newly issued tokens. They receive dollars back when they redeem the tokens. DBS and Circle described settlement of both conversions as near-instant, including outside normal banking hours and cutoff times.

Evy Theunis, head of digital assets for DBS’ institutional banking group, said:

“Institutions are increasingly looking to tokenized money to manage liquidity more efficiently and support their growth across new markets.”

An eligible company that uses blockchain-based cross-border payments could obtain USDC when it needs tokens for settlement and redeem unused tokens to replenish its dollar balance.

Around-the-Clock Treasury Services Expand at DBS

A DBS survey of 422 executives across 11 markets, published Oct. 28, found that 88% of the businesses surveyed were using or testing tokenized money. Respondents came from companies with annual revenue above $500 million. In their partnership announcement, DBS and Circle said more than three in five of those businesses were adopting stablecoins or planned to do so.

On Nov. 16, DBS and Kinexys by J.P. Morgan launched ’round-the-clock transfers of tokenized dollar deposits between blockchain-based accounts in Singapore and the United States. The 24/7 schedule applies to transfers between the blockchain-based accounts. Transfers between Kinexys and traditional accounts have a three-hour Saturday interruption. Ant International was the first client to use the service, which lets its treasury teams shift dollar balances between the two markets.

DBS also worked with Citi on a weekend U.S. dollar transfer using tokenized deposits between Singapore and the United States in September. The payment went through the Swift Digital Ledger.

Singapore Tests How Different Forms of Digital Money Can Work Together

DBS and Circle both participate in Project BLOOM, a public-private initiative led by the Monetary Authority of Singapore. The project examines how banks and payment networks can accept and settle transactions using different forms of digital money, including tokenized commercial bank deposits and stablecoins that meet regulatory expectations. One goal is to align commercial and operating arrangements so financial institutions have less need to set up separate arrangements with each counterparty or market.

On Nov. 16, the Monetary Authority of Singapore and Germany’s central bank reported a successful cross-border settlement test with DBS and Deutsche Bank. The trial used wholesale central bank digital currencies to settle euro and Singapore dollar transactions across the central banks’ test environments.

Circle and DBS Have Each Struck Earlier Deals in Singapore

In 2024, Paxos named DBS its primary Singapore banking partner when the country’s central bank authorized the company’s local entity to offer digital payment token services. The bank’s role included cash management and custody of stablecoin reserves.

Circle also announced an agreement to buy Singapore-based payments provider Tazapay in September. The transaction still needs regulatory approvals, including clearance from the Monetary Authority of Singapore, and is expected to close in 2027.

summary: A German court has proposed dropping tax evasion and money laundering charges against the main defendant in exchange for 40,000 bitcoin—approximately $2.5 billion worth—and $41.67 million in victim compensation. Defendant Could Retain Nearly $1B in Bitcoin A high-profile German trial involving billi...

Published:Nov 18, 2026, 5:45 PM EST

A German court has proposed dropping tax evasion and money laundering charges against the main defendant in exchange for 40,000 bitcoin—approximately $2.5 billion worth—and $41.67 million in victim compensation.

WRITTEN BY

SHARE

Published: Nov 18, 2026, 5:45 PM EST

Key Takeaways

  • A German court offered to drop charges against the Movie2k defendant in exchange for 40,000 BTC.
  • The Movie2k defendant could still hold nearly $1 billion in bitcoin afterwards, based on his believed holdings.
  • The trial resumes Dec. 3 as defendants consider settlements involving bitcoin and cash.

Defendant Could Retain Nearly $1B in Bitcoin

A high-profile German trial involving billions of dollars in proceeds from the defunct illegal streaming portal Movie2k could conclude before the end of the year after a judge offered the main defendant a plea deal worth about $2.55 billion.

According to a local report, the presiding judge at the Leipzig Regional Court proposed dropping tax evasion and money laundering charges against the 43-year-old primary defendant in exchange for 40,000 bitcoin, currently valued near $2.5 billion.

Under the terms of the proposed agreement, the defendant would also be required to pay $41.67 million in compensation to potential victims. Should the unnamed defendant surrender nearly three-quarters of his known holdings, the defendant is expected to retain nearly $1 billion worth of bitcoin. Investigators believe he still controls approximately 56,000 bitcoin in total.

The court also presented a settlement offer to a co-defendant, requiring him to forfeit 600 bitcoins and pay $18.6 million. His defense attorney indicated she could envision her client accepting the terms. Lawyers for the main defendant said they plan to consult with one another before responding.

The trial is scheduled to resume Dec. 3.

Authorities dismantled the Movie2k streaming portal in 2013 after years of widespread copyright violations. Prosecutors allege in the indictment that the site’s operators built a lucrative online piracy hub, illegally offering hundreds of thousands of pirated films to millions of viewers before converting the illicit proceeds into bitcoin.

Following his arrest in 2023, the main defendant surrendered about 50,400 bitcoin to investigators. Authorities subsequently sold the digital assets for approximately $2.90 billion, which are currently being held in escrow by the state treasury. Two other individuals connected to the operation have already been convicted.

Binance says it obtained $6.5 billion worldwide freezing order after hack

Binance said it has secured a $6.5 billion worldwide freezing injunction from the Abu Dhabi Global Market Courts as it seeks to recover assets stolen in its record Oct. 29 hack.

The court orders target unidentified perpetrators of the attack and are intended to help issuers, exchanges and other partners freeze and return stolen assets, the company said in a statement shared with Cointelegraph on Wednesday.

The orders can be served via blockchain, according to M. Kendall Day of Gibson Dunn, which represents Binance. This allows legal notices to be delivered to wallet addresses rather than through traditional channels. Day said market participants would also be notified of updates to a “living list” of 26,000 wallet addresses identified as holding stolen assets.

Binance said some businesses require formal court orders before they can release, transfer or return frozen funds. The injunction’s $6.5 billion amount is not a tally of recovered assets, and the statement did not disclose how much had so far been returned under the orders.

Binance also said it obtained orders requiring stolen assets to be handed over. Separate interim orders cover assets frozen by certain named parties against whom no wrongdoing is alleged.

Tokenized Nvidia market cap surges 159% amid Jensen Huang’s exit

The combined market value of tokenized stocks tied to Nvidia shares rose about 159% from Nov. 8 to Tuesday, while the chipmaker’s Nasdaq-listed shares fell nearly 17% from their last close before co-founder Jensen Huang publicly admitted to an extramarital affair.

The value of Nvidia (NVDA) tokens tracked by Token Terminal rose from $155 million on Nov. 8 to $401.9 million by Tuesday.

Nvidia shed about $750 billion in market value, falling from $4.5 trillion at the Nov. 6 close to $3.75 trillion at Tuesday’s close, according to Yahoo Finance data.

Huang acknowledged the affair in a message to Nvidia employees on Nov. 8, nearly two weeks after The New York Times reported that US intelligence officials suspected Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang of spying for Beijing. China denied the allegations.

Tokenized stocks are blockchain tokens designed to track the price of a share. In one common setup, an issuer creates tokens backed by shares held by a custodian.

Binance, for example, lists an Nvidia token that can trade when Nasdaq is closed. It gives investors exposure to Nvidia’s share price without shareholder rights. The market value can rise as more tokens enter circulation, even if Nvidia’s share price falls.

Ledger hardware implant saga reaches Dubai’s Virgin Megastore

Two Ledger owners have reported cryptocurrency thefts involving hardware wallets they say were purchased from an authorized retailer in Dubai, raising concerns that a hardware wallet tampering campaign had also spread to the UAE.

An X user posting as Rewinsky on Monday said they found their Ledger Flex had been tampered with after reporting the loss of about 1,300 Solana (SOL) Mark Karpelès’ Ledger Implant OSINT registry subsequently confirmed the device as containing a hardware implant.

A second owner, posting as New Babylon Order Worldwide, said Tuesday that 507,000 USDt (USDT) was stolen from their Ledger Stax on Saturday. They said the device was bought new at Virgin Megastore Dubai on Oct. 11, two days after Ledger publicly disclosed an investigation into crypto losses involving devices sold by Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis.

The reports suggest the Ledger device tampering has extended past retailers in just Asia and Europe. Ledger lists Virgin Megastores among its authorized retailers in the United Arab Emirates.

title: Tether invokes The Big Short in swipe at S&P over USDT reserve risks
summary: S&P Global made no downward adjustment in its latest Stablecoin Stability Assessment, as 5 is the lowest available score.
content:
S&P Global Ratings has kept Tether’s USDt at the lowest level on its stablecoin stability scale as riskier assets take up a growing share of the token’s reserves.

In a report published Nov. 18, S&P scored USDt’s ability to hold its dollar peg at 5 (weak). The assessment is unchanged from November 2025.

Higher-risk holdings, including gold, Bitcoin (BTC), public equities, secured loans and corporate bonds, were equivalent to 28% of USDt (USDT) in circulation as of Sept. 30, up from 24% a year earlier. “A significant drop in the value of these assets could lead to USDT being undercollateralized,” S&P said in the report.

“The problem is S&P’s framework, not our reserves,” Tether told Cointelegraph. “Their own history shows the underlying problem,” it added, referencing The Big Short, the film about the 2008 financial crisis.

Tether’s Sept. 30 reserve report, attested by BDO, showed approximately $191.5 billion in assets against $183.5 billion in liabilities, leaving roughly $7.95 billion in excess assets. The agency added that it found further weaknesses but made no downward adjustment “because our assessment cannot be lower than 5.”

S&P questions reserve oversight safeguards

Among the additional weaknesses highlighted by S&P was the regulatory oversight of El Salvador, where Tether relocated in January 2025.

According to the report, the National Commission of Digital Assets of El Salvador (CNAD), the regulatory body which oversees Tether in the country, requires 70% of the reserves to be held in assets that can be liquidated within 30 days. The company said they considered the framework “broad,” allowing for the inclusion of relatively high-risk assets like gold, BTC and loans.

The S&P also pointed to the lack of a requirement to segregate the reserve assets, unlike those expected by regulators in the US and Europe. As there is no publicly available information about segregation, the report states, there is no insight into how they are insulated from broader corporate risks.

USDT’s breakdown of reserve assets. Source S&P Global

Audit disclosure remains a concern

In August 2026, KPMG confirmed they had issued an unqualified opinion on Tether’s 2025 accounts, in the company’s first “full independent audit”. The issuer highlighted that the audit supported the financial statements issued by the company.

However, S&P said the audited statements and the auditor’s report have not been published, which limits its ability to check the underlying information. Reserve reports also do not name the custodians and counterparties holding Tether’s assets, S&P said, and attestations remain quarterly while other stablecoins generally report monthly.

Related: Tether backs Bolivian fintech bringing USDT payments to food delivery and banking

At the time of S&P’s initial downgrade in 2025, Tether disputed the result. CEO Paolo Ardoino wrote on X, “we wear your loathing with pride,” pointing to past financial collapses as “proof” that traditional systems are broken.

Although the stability rating remained at 5, S&P ended the Nov. 18 report noting that Tether had maintained a good history of price stability, particularly in the last 12 months.

title: Bitcoin Price Worst-Case Scenarios: Analysts Talk $50K, $40K and $10K
summary: As bitcoin erased all of its post-August gains, bullish near-term sentiment is changing rapidly, too. Worst-case bitcoin price scenarios range from the $50,000s in the near term to $10,000 if stocks crash, while the evergreen calls for “BTC going to zero” remain. content:
As bitcoin erased all of its post-August gains, bullish near-term sentiment is changing rapidly, too. Worst-case bitcoin price scenarios range from the $50,000s in the near term to $10,000 if stocks crash, while the evergreen calls for “BTC going to zero” remain. However, the reality is more complicated. Dominant market sentiment has often proved to be a poor predictor of price action.

Key Takeaways

  • Bitcoin analysts identify $58,000-$62,000 as the next crucial support range, with $50,000 and $40,000 downside scenarios.
  • Bearish sentiment is growing, with ETF outflows, inflation, and rate-hike risks weighing on market outlooks.
  • Some analysts see signs of a local bottom, but warn that recovery could involve prolonged consolidation.

Bitcoin.com News examined multiple estimates by bitcoin analysts and found that many agree that bitcoin’s next crucial test is the $58,000-62,000 range.

A familiar pattern emerges in these predictions: Analysts identify a level to watch and, if it breaks or a specific event occurs, set their next downside target. For example, crypto market maker Wintermute identifies the weekend’s $62,000 low as the first level to watch, followed by a cluster of $60,000 put options on Deribit.

With ETF flows negative and bitcoin below its 200-week moving average, it expects “pressure into the $50s.” Others argue that under specific conditions, BTC could fall toward $40,000 or lower.

Bitcoin Bears Are Multiplying

Cryptoquant’s Analyst Consensus page shows that bearish narratives now outnumber bullish ones, 16 to 10, although bullish analysts still slightly outnumber their bearish counterparts. As usual, bears and bulls point to different signals to support their predictions.

As of Nov. 18, bearish analysts tracked by Cryptoquant mostly focused on ETF outflows, hacks, inflation, and the risk of another Fed rate hike. Meanwhile, bulls pointed to oversold signals, bottom indicators, and institutional buying. However, at this stage, it is unclear which signals will carry more weight and determine near- to medium-term price action.

On Nov. 18, 85 analysts tracked by Cryptoquant were bullish and 75 were bearish, meaning about 53% retained positive outlooks. That was 11 percentage points below the page’s 30-day average of 64%. On Oct. 6, bulls outnumbered bears 136 to 21. For comparison, in mid-August, just before the rally that took BTC from about $63,000 to about $87,000, 59% of analysts were bullish.

“Bitcoin still trades largely as a high-beta liquidity asset. An environment like this could trigger cascading leveraged liquidations if Bitcoin breaks below $60,000-$62,000, likely pushing the price towards the mid-$50,000s,” Salman Parcy, managing partner of Cequire Capital, told Bitcoin.com News. In their risk modeling, the worst-case scenario for BTC in the near-to-medium term is a prolonged period of tight liquidity and tightening of macro conditions, such as renewed inflation.

How Bitcoin’s Price Could Drop to $40K

Now, both sentiment and analysts’ predictions are catching up with the price. Mignolet, the founder of onchain intelligence platform Foredex, prefaced his latest analysis by calling it “a scenario that I considered only a remote possibility earlier this year.” He added that this scenario, as the indicators he tracks deteriorate, “deserves serious consideration as a potential worst-case outcome for bitcoin.”

According to him, if the U.S. dollar keeps strengthening, the U.S. stock market falls and Binance whales keep selling BTC, then the price “could decline into the low-$40,000 range under my worst-case scenario.”

Mignolet describes this area as miners’ “Operational Floor Cost” and calls it “a critical level that needs to hold.” Otherwise, “the financial stability and long-term viability of some publicly listed mining companies could come under serious pressure.” In either case, the founder emphasized that this is his worst-case scenario, not a prediction he is certain will come true.

Not the Best Time for Another Shock

The analyst also warned that if the three conditions mentioned above persist, then BTC could enter a much deeper long-term correction. Bitcoin is already at risk of ending the year down, which would mark the first time in its history that it has recorded two consecutive annual losses.

“The bitcoin market has still not gone through sufficient accumulation, and liquidity conditions continue to deteriorate. At this point, we can only hope the market avoids a major shock,” Mignolet said in a separate post.

Meanwhile, Rekt Capital, another popular crypto asset investor and analyst, said that it did not appear that a “sequence of bearish retests is over just yet.” He also added that “consistent sell-side capitulation is unsustainable and can’t last forever.”

According to the analyst, BTC needs to avoid a weekly close below support at about $63,300 to prevent further downside toward $59,443. A weekly close above about $65,700 would end the sequence. Bitcoin’s weekly close last week was about $65,350, between the two levels.

Before the weekend slide, on Nov. 11, Glassnode also noted that bitcoin’s “biggest liquidation cluster sits near $60k,” made up of long positions opened near the bottom before August’s rally. It added that “patient buyers have often found opportunity in forced selling, and a sweep of $60k would create plenty of it.”

Some patient buyers might also be watching Bloomberg Intelligence’s Mike McGlone’s call for BTC to crash to $10,000, particularly if the U.S. stock market falls 20%. In response, Ki Young Ju, CEO of Cryptoquant, argued that bitcoin would not fall that far, placing bitcoin’s onchain price floor near $30,000.

Contrarian Cautious Optimists and No Guarantees

Looking at Cryptoquant’s BTC price and sentiment chart, it appears that sentiment usually follows the price and can reinforce the trend, as it appears to be doing now.

However, there are always contrarians who might still be right. In this case, some argue that BTC has already bottomed or will soon do so.

For example, K33 Research’s Vetle Lunde analyzed bitcoin’s 200-week moving average, ETF flows, capital outflows, and derivatives market positioning. He concluded that the data suggests BTC may have formed a local bottom. However, like Mignolet, Lunde warned that previous recoveries from similar levels involved prolonged consolidation, pointing to “a choppy recovery rather than an immediate rebound.”

Meanwhile, Bitwise CIO Matt Hougan, like Wintermute, blamed the sell-off on rising rates, specifically the jump in rate-hike expectations after a hot October inflation report. He said this shock had now played out, leaving him “cautiously optimistic,” although he noted there was no guarantee of a recovery.

To conclude, one thing is certain in the bitcoin market: After the price crashes or moons, everyone will “know” why it happened. Do your own research and don’t invest more than you can afford to lose.

title: Ledger warns Berlin customers as hardware wallet tampering investigation expands
summary: Ledger advised customers who purchased devices in Berlin since January 2026 to contact support as it investigates suspected hardware implants in Germany and Dubai.
content:
Latest NewsPublishedNov 18, 2026

Ledger advised customers who purchased devices in Berlin since January 2026 to contact support as it investigates suspected hardware implants in Germany and Dubai.

Ledger has warned customers who purchased hardware wallets in Berlin since January 2026 to contact its support team as the company investigates reports of tampered devices in Germany and the United Arab Emirates.

In a Wednesday update, Ledger said its investigation into a hardware wallet tampering campaign had identified several suspicious devices in Berlin. The company also acknowledged reports of tampered devices in Dubai, where two customers recently reported losing a combined $604,000 in cryptocurrency.

Ledger said the incidents were connected to the same distribution-channel tampering campaign first investigated in Southeast Asia in October, when the company asked authorized reseller CryptoBilis to suspend sales and shipments amid reports of cryptocurrency thefts. Ledger also confirmed that one Ledger Nano Gen 5 had been affected in the region.

According to the hardware wallet maker, all confirmed tampered devices contained similar physical modifications designed to capture users’ recovery phrases during setup. The company said it had found no vulnerability in its secure chip or operating system and no confirmed cases involving devices purchased directly from its website.

Ledger is also offering physical inspections, including X-ray analysis, at its factory in Vierzon, France, for customers concerned their devices may have been compromised.

title: Bain Capital Crypto leads $110M Variational round at $1.5B valuation
summary: Variational raised $110 million at a $1.5 billion valuation to expand Omni’s derivatives markets and increase trading limits.
content:
Onchain derivatives trading platform Variational has raised $110 million in a funding round led by Bain Capital Crypto, valuing the company at $1.5 billion as it seeks to challenge traditional brokerages by connecting crypto traders with liquidity from established financial markets.

The Series B round also received backing from Dragonfly, HSG, Peak XV and 50T Funds, according to the company’s Wednesday announcement.

Variational powers Omni, a platform offering leveraged exposure to more than 550 crypto and traditional markets. Unlike Hyperliquid, which maintains separate order books for its markets, Variational aggregates liquidity from onchain and off-chain sources, including Hyperliquid itself, a company spokesperson told Cointelegraph.

“Our unique model allows us to bridge off-chain liquidity to on-chain traders,” the spokesperson said, adding that liquidity from its unnamed tier-one market maker remains off-chain.

Since launching in early 2025, Omni has processed more than $475 billion in trading volume across over 100,000 accounts, the company said. Traditional markets now account for more than half of its daily trading volume.

Variational also launched its swaps product in September, which has since generated more than $80 billion in trading volume, according to the company.

Variational looks to compete with traditional brokerages

Despite traditional assets accounting for most daily trading volume, Variational’s customers remain primarily crypto-native retail traders, a company spokesperson told Cointelegraph. Asked about competing with traditional brokerages such as Robinhood and Interactive Brokers, the spokesperson pointed to the need to make the platform more accessible to users unfamiliar with cryptocurrency.

Related: Hyperliquid Strategies seeks futures registration for perps

“The platform needs to abstract away the ‘crypto’ feel,” the spokesperson said, adding that the company is developing email-based account registration and alternative deposit methods to remove the current requirements for crypto wallets and USDC.

Variational faces stiff competition in onchain derivatives trading. Hyperliquid recorded approximately $274 billion in reported trading volume over the past 30 days, compared with $82 billion for Lighter and $62 billion for Variational, according to DeFiLlama data at the time of writing on Wednesday. Variational also ranked third in open interest at approximately $688 million, behind Hyperliquid’s $5.7 billion and Aster’s $1.2 billion.

title: Ondo to Launch Tokenized Anthropic Stock as IPO Demand Nears $500 Billion
summary: Ondo Finance plans to offer around-the-clock exposure to Anthropic shares as the AI giant reportedly considers expanding its IPO and pricing shares above $80 amid overwhelming investor demand. Ondo Finance announced Wednesday that it will launch a tokenized version of Anthropic stock alongside the a...
content:
Ondo Finance plans to offer around-the-clock exposure to Anthropic shares as the AI giant reportedly considers expanding its IPO and pricing shares above $80 amid overwhelming investor demand.

Key Takeaways

  • Ondo Finance plans to launch ANTon, a tokenized version of Anthropic stock, alongside the AI company’s anticipated Nasdaq debut on Nov. 19, offering eligible non-U.S. investors 24/7 minting and redemption.
  • Anthropic’s IPO is reportedly attracting nearly $500 billion in investor demand, including approximately $400 billion from institutions and $100 billion from retail investors. CNBC reports that the company may expand its offering and price shares above $80.
  • Ondo continues expanding its tokenized securities platform, which offers more than 450 tokenized stocks and ETFs and has surpassed $1 billion in total value locked.

Ondo Finance announced Wednesday that it will launch a tokenized version of Anthropic stock alongside the artificial intelligence company’s highly anticipated initial public offering (IPO), as reports suggest investor demand for the listing is approaching $500 billion.

The new asset, called ANTon, will be available through Ondo Stocks when Anthropic begins trading on Nasdaq, currently scheduled for Thursday, Nov. 19. Ondo said the token will support around-the-clock minting and redemption from its first day, including weekends and holidays, subject to maintenance and occasional interruptions.

Eligible investors outside the United States will be able to gain exposure starting at $1, with no minting fees and reduced redemption fees, although blockchain network fees will still apply. Ondo said ANTon will be backed by underlying securities, but emphasized that the product is independent of Anthropic and is not part of the company’s IPO.

Ondo isn’t the only crypto firm seeking to capitalize on Anthropic’s blockbuster IPO. Binance Wallet launched an eight-hour sale Wednesday for up to $500 million in tokenized Anthropic shares through xStocks, with a minimum investment of 100 USDC and a 5% fee. The tokens, called ANTx, are issued by Backed or its affiliates and provide price exposure without direct share ownership, voting rights, or dividend entitlements.

Kraken has also opened requests for ANTx tokens in eligible markets, underscoring growing competition among crypto platforms to offer access to one of the year’s most anticipated stock listings.

Anthropic IPO Demand Approaches $500 Billion

Anthropic is reportedly considering increasing the size of its offering as institutional and retail investors scramble for shares in what could become the largest IPO in history.

According to a Wednesday CNBC report, institutional investors have submitted approximately $400 billion in orders, while retail demand is approaching $100 billion. The figures represent nonbinding indications of interest rather than confirmed purchases.

Anthropic initially planned to offer 825 million shares at $70 to $78 apiece, potentially raising $64.35 billion at the upper end of that range. However, the company is now weighing an expansion of the offering and could set the final share price substantially above $80, CNBC reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

The AI developer is expected to finalize pricing Wednesday afternoon, with shares scheduled to begin trading Thursday under the ticker ANT. The reported demand exceeds that generated by SpaceX’s blockbuster IPO, which raised approximately $85.7 billion earlier this year.

Anthropic’s amended IPO filing revealed $33.24 billion in revenue during the first nine months of 2026, an increase of approximately 1,200% from the comparable period a year earlier. The developer of the Claude AI assistant also reported a $104 billion net loss, largely reflecting accounting adjustments related to convertible notes and derivative liabilities.

The company disclosed an annualized revenue run rate of approximately $81 billion at the end of October, up $10 billion from September, highlighting the extraordinary pace of its growth.

Ondo Expands Tokenized Stock Platform

Ondo said ANTon will join more than 450 tokenized stocks and exchange-traded funds (ETFs) already available through its platform, which has surpassed $1 billion in total value locked (TVL). Its products are available across Ethereum, Solana, and BNB Chain.

Unlike traditional shares, ANTon tokens provide economic exposure to the underlying stock rather than direct ownership. Ondo’s terms specify that holders do not receive the underlying securities themselves, making the distinction particularly important for investors seeking conventional shareholder rights.

The company’s latest offering builds on an aggressive expansion of its tokenized securities business. Ondo Global Markets expanded to Solana in January with more than 200 tokenized U.S. stocks and ETFs. It subsequently integrated with Binance Alpha in February, expanding international access to blockchain-based versions of major equities, including Apple, Nvidia, and Tesla.

In July, Ondo also announced the tokenization of Blackrock’s iShares Core S&P 500 ETF and Micron shares under a U.S. regulatory structure, with Broadridge Financial Solutions providing shareholder communications and proxy voting services.

The planned ANTon debut comes amid growing competition to bring traditional equities onto blockchain networks. Tokenization providers are increasingly targeting investors seeking access to U.S. securities beyond conventional trading hours, although the underlying stock markets continue to operate on established exchange schedules.

Ondo’s latest announcement takes that competition to one of the year’s most closely watched public listings, testing whether extraordinary demand for a major technology IPO can also drive interest in tokenized equities.

The company stressed that ANTon will not be available to U.S. investors under its current offering framework, while additional eligibility restrictions apply in certain international jurisdictions.

title: Binance says it obtained $6.5B worldwide freezing order after hack
summary: The court orders allow legal notices to be served via blockchain and provide for a continuously updated list of 26,000 wallet addresses linked to stolen assets, Binance’s lawyers said.
content:
Binance said it has secured a $6.5 billion worldwide freezing injunction from the Abu Dhabi Global Market Courts as it seeks to recover assets stolen in its record Oct. 29 hack.

The court orders target unidentified perpetrators of the attack and are intended to help issuers, exchanges and other partners freeze and return stolen assets, the company said in a statement shared with Cointelegraph on Wednesday.

The orders can be served via blockchain, according to M. Kendall Day of Gibson Dunn, which represents Binance. This allows legal notices to be delivered to wallet addresses rather than through traditional channels. Day said market participants would also be notified of updates to a “living list” of 26,000 wallet addresses identified as holding stolen assets.

Binance said some businesses require formal court orders before they can release, transfer or return frozen funds. The injunction’s $6.5 billion amount is not a tally of recovered assets, and the statement did not disclose how much had so far been returned under the orders.

Binance also said it obtained orders requiring stolen assets to be handed over. Separate interim orders cover assets frozen by certain named parties against whom no wrongdoing is alleged.

Binance pursues stolen asset recovery

The legal action follows other efforts to secure the stolen funds in the wake of the hack, the largest-ever in the crypto industry. As Cointelegraph reported on Nov. 13, the US Justice Department said it had obtained court authorization to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion in assets stolen from Binance. That amount was part of more than $2.7 billion frozen through government and private sector efforts, the DOJ said.

Related: Binance hack may push institutions to outside custody, FalconX exec says

As Cointelegraph previously reported, the attackers converted stolen stablecoins into assets such as Bitcoin (BTC) and Ether (ETH), which cannot be frozen, as they lack a central issuer. Blocking the stolen tokens also does not mean they’ll be returned to Binance.

Binance said last week it had since completed coverage of affected assets after committing more than $6.34 billion from its various treasury, Secure Asset Fund for Users and insurance funds. Still, replenishing customer assets is separate from recovering the stolen cryptocurrencies from the hack.

Related: North Korea denies role in $6.3B Binance hack, points finger at US

Binance pursues expansion across Asia

Separately, Binance’s Asia-Pacific head SB Seker told Reuters on Wednesday that the exchange plans to enter five Asian markets in 2027, prioritizing South and Southeast Asia. He did not name the markets and said details were expected in the first quarter.

Seker also said Binance did not need fresh capital to absorb the losses from the October hack.

title: Coinshares Sells All Ether, Half Its Solana to Fund $40M Share Buyback
summary: Coinshares sold its entire corporate ether position and half of its solana holdings, freeing $19.3 million for a share repurchase program of up to $40 million. Coinshares Shifts From ETH, SOL to Its Own Stock Coinshares is turning part of its crypto treasury into cash and directing the proceeds towa...
content:
Coinshares sold its entire corporate ether position and half of its solana holdings, freeing $19.3 million for a share repurchase program of up to $40 million.

Key Takeaways

  • Coinshares sold all corporate ETH and half its SOL, freeing $19.3M for a $40M buyback.
  • Q3 net income hit $39.6M despite revenue falling 44.9% YoY to $27.7M.
  • The shift suggests Coinshares sees its own stock as a better use of capital than holding more crypto.

Coinshares Shifts From ETH, SOL to Its Own Stock

Coinshares is turning part of its crypto treasury into cash and directing the proceeds toward its own stock.

The digital asset manager sold $16.6 million of ether and $2.7 million of solana, representing all of its corporate ETH and half of its SOL holdings, according to its Q3 results released on Wednesday. The sales generated $19.3 million, nearly half of the $40 million share repurchase authorization approved by its board in October.

“We sold our entire corporate treasury position in [ether] and half of our corporate treasury position in solana,” CEO Jean-Marie Mognetti said. “That’s nearly half of the $40 million authorized by the board and gives us the flexibility to act when conditions allow.”

Profit Rebounds Despite 45% Revenue Decline

Coinshares posted $39.6 million in Q3 net income, reversing a $13.6 million loss in the previous quarter and rising 27% from $31.2 million a year earlier.

Revenue told a different story. Quarterly revenue fell 44.9% year over year to $27.7 million, reflecting weaker digital asset prices and lower average assets under management. Segment EBITDA dropped to $20.6 million from $53.3 million a year ago. A $14.4 million gain on treasury digital assets helped lift net income.

AUM Returns to $7.4 Billion

Coinshares’ assets under management recovered to $7.4 billion at the end of September from $5.5 billion three months earlier, returning to the same level reported at the end of 2025.

The rebound came from both higher crypto prices and $125 million of quarterly net inflows.

Coinshares Physical, its European investment-product platform, attracted $77.8 million during the quarter, while total nine-month company inflows reached $152.6 million.

Capital-markets performance also improved. Revenue and gains from that segment rose to $17.8 million from $4.9 million in Q2, helped by stronger lending and trading.

Crypto Treasury Becomes Buyback Ammunition

The ETH and SOL sales highlight a notable capital-allocation shift.

Rather than keeping all of its liquid capital exposed to crypto assets, Coinshares is using part of its treasury to potentially support its own share price.

The company ended September with $492.4 million in net assets, $452.7 million of available capital, and no long-term debt.

For shareholders, that creates a clear trade-off. Coinshares is giving up some direct upside from ether and solana in exchange for flexibility to repurchase stock when management believes the valuation is attractive.

In a volatile crypto market, the move suggests Coinshares sees its own shares as another asset worth buying.

title: Scattered Spider Hacker Gets Six Years for $11.6 Million Crypto Theft
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Scattered Spider Hacker Gets Six Years for $11.6 Million Crypto Theft
A Scottish hacker tied to Scattered Spider was sentenced to six years in U.S. prison for a SIM-swap and phishing scheme that stole at least $11.6 million in crypto.
This post Scattered Spider Hacker Gets Six Year...
content:
A Scottish hacker tied to the Scattered Spider group was sentenced to six years in U.S. federal prison on Tuesday for a text-message phishing and SIM-swapping scheme that stole at least $11.6 million in crypto, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Central District of California said.

Tyler Robert Buchanan, 24, of Dundee, Scotland, received a 72-month sentence from U.S. District Judge John W. Holcomb in Santa Ana. He had pleaded guilty in April to conspiracy to commit wire fraud and aggravated identity theft. A restitution hearing is set for Dec. 11.

Prosecutors did not say which cryptocurrencies were taken, and the release does not break the haul down by coin. Buchanan is the fifth and final defendant to be sentenced in the case, closing out a prosecution of a hacker crew that the Justice Department charged together.

How the scheme worked

From September 2021 to April 2023, Buchanan and his co-conspirators sent hundreds of phishing texts to employees of at least a dozen companies, prosecutors said. The messages posed as the employer or one of its IT contractors and linked to fake login pages that captured usernames, passwords and other personal information.

The group then used the stolen data to run SIM swaps, which move a victim’s phone number to a SIM card the attacker controls. That gave them a way into victims’ virtual currency accounts and wallets. The BBC reported that Buchanan set up a Telegram bot to collect the credentials as workers handed them over.

The largest single theft, according to prosecutors, was $1.67 million taken from one victim in December 2022. Prosecutors said the thefts had “severe, life-altering consequences” for victims.

The BBC said the money came from individual victims rather than from the companies whose employees were phished. Prosecutors first put the hacker group’s take at about $8 million, and the $11.6 million figure is the loss authorities calculated for the full scheme.

From Scotland to a California courtroom

Police Scotland searched Buchanan’s bedroom in April 2023 after a request from the FBI, the BBC said. Investigators found a device holding the names and addresses of victims, along with crypto seed phrases and account credentials belonging to at least one victim.

Buchanan left the U.K. the following month. Spanish authorities arrested him at Palma de Mallorca Airport in 2024 as he tried to board a private flight to Naples.

Bloomberg News reported, and Reuters relayed, that he was extradited from Spain in April 2025. He was charged with wire fraud and aggravated identity theft alongside four other alleged Scattered Spider members, and he has been in U.S. custody since.

What Scattered Spider is

Reuters has described Scattered Spider as a loose-knit community of hackers suspected of breaking into dozens of U.S. companies. The DOJ release does not use the group’s name, but the BBC says Buchanan, a teenage hacker when the campaign began, was a member and a Justice Department spokesperson has previously tied the defendants to it.

The BBC said Buchanan’s four co-defendants have all pleaded guilty and are serving time. It described the case as a years-long investigation involving authorities in the U.K., the U.S., Spain and Canada.

Scattered Spider has also faced prosecution in Britain. Two other members were jailed in the U.K. in July for a series of attacks, including one on Transport for London that caused £39 million in damage, the BBC said.

The judge will set the amount of restitution at a hearing on Dec. 11, the final step in the case against the Scottish hacker.

title: Binance Says It Won Court Order to Recover Frozen Hack Funds
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Binance Says It Won Court Order to Recover Frozen Hack Funds
Binance says it has a court order from Abu Dhabi Global Market to recover crypto frozen after the $6.3 billion hack.
This post Binance Says It Won Court Order to Recover Frozen Hack Funds first appeared on Bitcoin Magazin...
content:
Binance says it has secured a court order from Abu Dhabi Global Market to help it recover crypto frozen after the record $6.3 billion hack last month, Reuters reported on Wednesday. The exchange has not said how much of the money the order covers.

Reuters described Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM) as Binance’s main financial regulator. Binance deputy general counsel Dugan Bliss confirmed the order in a statement but gave no details on its terms. Neither the company nor Reuters said which assets it applies to.

“We will continue using every lawful tool available to trace, freeze and recover stolen assets, support our partners in returning funds where possible, and keep those assets out of the hands of the attackers,” Bliss said.

What is frozen

Binance has said about $2.85 billion of the stolen tokens were frozen or intercepted after the Oct. 29 attack, according to its own incident report. That is roughly 45% of the $6.34 billion it says was affected.

Most of it sits with stablecoin issuers. Tether said it froze more than $1.5 billion in USDT within 30 minutes of the attack, and Circle said it froze about $1.1 billion in USDC in coordination with law enforcement. Circle added that it does not decide who owns frozen assets, a question it left to law enforcement and the courts.

The Justice Department has separately obtained court authority to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion of the stolen crypto. It is part of more than $2.7 billion that Justice says government and private-sector efforts have frozen. Criminal Division head A. Tysen Duva said the department helped “immediately halt about half of this historic breach.” Reuters did not say how the ADGM order fits with the U.S. action.

How the hack unfolded

Binance says the attack began months earlier, with a tampered software installer that compromised one engineer in June. In September, another engineer was approached by a fake recruiter and persuaded to run a bogus interview assignment that installed malware, the company said.

From there, the attackers reached an internal wallet-signing service and drained Binance hot wallets across multiple blockchains on Oct. 29. The thefts included 233.46 million XRP, about 970,500 SOL and 18,270 BTC, according to Binance.

The FBI has attributed the theft to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group, and Binance has said the same. Pyongyang denies involvement. Blockchain analysts said the attacker tried to outrun the freezes by swapping stablecoins into ether over about 20 minutes, but the issuers moved faster.

That split matters for bitcoin. Tether and Circle can block their own tokens, but bitcoin has no issuer. The stolen BTC is not covered by those freezes and can be stopped only if it reaches an exchange or service that blocks it.

Binance says it can absorb the loss

Binance has already said it replaced the affected assets with company funds, using part of its SAFU emergency fund and its corporate treasury. Withdrawals resumed in phases earlier this month, and the exchange aims to reopen all remaining networks and assets by the end of this week, Reuters reported.

On Wednesday, Binance’s Asia-Pacific head SB Seker told Reuters at the Singapore FinTech Festival that the company plans to expand into five Asian markets in 2027 and does not need to raise new funds. He said talks are under way with five or six markets, three of them at a mature stage, and details are due in the first quarter.

Seker said the cost of replacing the stolen tokens was “statistically” not a large amount for the company. “In terms of the impact to us, we can take the impact and we can weather it without any change to the way we operate,” he said.

summary:
The Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) met its own service standards on only 54.5% of consumer investment applications, against 92.0% across all sectors, an FM Intelligence analysis published today (Wednesday) shows. The median case took 285 days.
The figures cover April to June 2026. Consumer invest...
content:
2026-11-18T20:31:00.000+02:00

Wednesday, 18/11/2026 | 18:31 GMT by Damian Chmiel

  • Consumer investment cases took a median 285 days in April to June 2026, and only 54.5% met FCA service standards.
  • FM Intelligence also counts 24 CFD firms closed or canceling since 2025 and puts first-year costs at £3.1 million to £11.0 million.

The Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) met its own service standards on only 54.5% of consumer investment applications, against 92.0% across all sectors, an FM Intelligence analysis published today (Wednesday) shows. The median case took 285 days.

The figures cover April to June 2026. Consumer investment is the FCA category closest to a new retail CFD broker, so that wait sets the start date for any firm entering Britain.

The FCA aims to decide 95% of cases within four months, or 10 if incomplete, against legal limits of six and 12. HM Treasury said in May 2026 it would cut the legal limits to match, though the legislation is not yet in force.

The market at the end of the wait is still large. The UK drew 13.9 million organic visits to broker websites in Q3 2026, more than any other European country, according to FM Intelligence's FX/CFD Heat Map.

Britons visited tracked broker sites about twice as often per person as Germans, the Featured Country: United Kingdom analysis finds.

London's trading industry is coming home!

Nine Months for a Typical Case

A quarter of consumer investment cases took more than 344 days, the regulator's service metrics show. Across all 287 new-firm cases closed in the quarter, the median was 131 days.

The wait carries a payroll, because an applicant has to show its senior managers and systems before approval. FM Intelligence's scenario keeps three to five key staff on the books for six to 10 months before launch, at £0.24 million (about $0.32 million) to £0.70 million.

Twenty-Four Firms Lost the FCA Halo

Buying a dormant UK firm is no shortcut. In December 2024 the FCA said about 20% of firms in its CFD portfolio did little or no business and served as "halo" entities for offshore groups. It said a change in control of such a firm would get the same scrutiny as a new application.

The same letter said none of the 100 CFD firms from the European Economic Area (EEA) that entered the post-Brexit temporary permissions regime in January 2021 had obtained full authorization.

On September 25, 2026, the regulator said 21 such firms had closed since 2025 and three more were canceling their permissions. It opened enforcement investigations in the two most serious cases and named none of the firms.

The 24 equal about a third of the 74 firms that held permission to sell CFDs to retail clients on December 1, 2025. The FCA did not say how many had retail permissions.

Some firms buy clients instead. Trade Nation agreed on October 6 to take over FXCM's UK client book, a deal for customers rather than for a license.

Marketing Is the Largest Cost

FM Intelligence puts first-year funding for a new UK broker at £3.1 million to £11.0 million before regulatory capital. The range compares a 10-person firm on coworking desks with a 15-person firm in a City office, and it is a planning scenario, not a quote.

Marketing makes up 48% to 64% of those first-year operating costs, including VAT. Plus500 and IG spent roughly £960 to £1,050 per new client in 2025.

The pool those budgets chase is smaller than it was. Investment Trends counted about 167,000 active UK leveraged traders in 2025, down from a peak of about 275,000 in 2021. The Heat Map tracks attention, not accounts, and does not cover IG or Spreadex.

The full FM Intelligence analysis sets out how many active clients a newcomer needs to cover its first-year costs, how IG's UK revenue splits between leveraged traders and investors, and the tax, staffing and capital lines behind the range.

title: MARA prices $185M debt offering after $1.1B Bitcoin sale
summary: The Bitcoin miner is taking on new debt to finance its AI infrastructure expansion, with the Long Ridge acquisition adding nearly $69 million in annual interest costs.
content:
Bitcoin miner MARA Holdings has priced a $185 million secured debt offering through its US subsidiary to help finance its $1.5 billion acquisition of Long Ridge Energy & Power.

According to a Tuesday filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission, the new notes carry an 8.75% interest rate and mature in 2032. They will be added to $600 million in existing Long Ridge notes carrying the same rate, bringing the combined principal to $785 million and annual interest obligations to around $68.7 million.

The offering is expected to close on Nov. 27, alongside MARA’s acquisition of Long Ridge, which operates a 485-megawatt natural gas power plant in Ohio. MARA announced the $1.5 billion acquisition on April 30 as part of its expansion into AI and high-performance computing infrastructure. The Long Ridge property includes land that MARA says could support more than 1 gigawatt of data center capacity, although the company has yet to announce a major AI tenant for the proposed development.

The financing follows MARA’s Nov. 9 disclosure that it sold 13,597 Bitcoin after quarter-end for approximately $1.1 billion. It used $750 million to repay Bitcoin (BTC)-backed loans, releasing 17,477 BTC previously pledged as collateral.

MARA’s debt reduction contrasts with AI financing costs

MARA has sold billions of dollars in Bitcoin this year to reduce its debt. In March, the company sold 15,133 BTC for approximately $1.1 billion, using the proceeds to help repurchase $1 billion in convertible notes at a roughly 9% discount, saving approximately $88 million before transaction costs.

In its Nov. 9 shareholder letter, MARA said it had reduced debt by approximately $1.4 billion, or 37%, since the beginning of the year. However, the Long Ridge acquisition will bring additional debt onto its consolidated balance sheet.

Related: Luxor raises $16M from CMT Digital amid AI-Bitcoin miner convergence

According to MARA’s April 30 acquisition announcement, Long Ridge generated approximately $144 million in annualized adjusted EBITDA, extrapolated from the second half of 2025. The roughly $68.7 million in annual interest payments on the secured notes would equal nearly half that figure.

MARA also faces potential debt repayments next year. According to its third-quarter 10-Q, holders of approximately $924 million in convertible notes have the right to demand repayment in 2027, potentially creating another cash requirement as the company finances its AI expansion.

MARA shares traded at $6.57 at 6:53 pm UTC on Wednesday, up 2.34% on the day, but down 46% over the past six months, according to Yahoo Finance data.

summary:
Grand Theft Auto VI has begun its global rollout, reaching players in Australia and New Zealand and bringing multimillion-dollar prediction markets on delays and release windows toward final resolution. 
But this is not the end of the story for the prediction market traders, rotating capital into th...

Wednesday, 18/11/2026 | 18:19 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Kalshi’s contract on whether GTA VI would launch on schedule drew more than $1.1 million in trading volume by November 18.
  • Traders are turning to contracts on review scores and first-week soundtrack sales, while separate markets track when a PC version might arrive.

Grand Theft Auto VI has begun its global rollout, reaching players in Australia and New Zealand and bringing multimillion-dollar prediction markets on delays and release windows toward final resolution.

But this is not the end of the story for the prediction market traders, rotating capital into the game’s commercial performance, review scores, soundtrack, and future PC release.

The Launch Closes the Biggest Question

The years of schedule uncertainty effectively turned Rockstar Games’ release calendar into a liquid hedging and speculation vehicle.

After Rockstar postponed the game to May 2026, Polymarket opened a contract on whether it would arrive before June. Rockstar pushed the date back again in November 2025, and the contract eventually settled No, having generated $15.25 million in trading volume

As Rockstar’s revised launch date approached, trading on Kalshi’s contract on whether GTA VI would be released by November 19 topped $1.1 million by November 18.

A separate Kalshi market covering several release deadlines, including whether the game would launch before 2027, had already drawn more than $7 million in trading volume by November 14, according to Game File.

Traders Move from Deadlines to Specific Outcomes

Once the November release date solidified, traders shifted from a single macro deadline to dozens of short-term outcomes tied to the game’s content.

Kalshi opened trading on which artists would appear on Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album the day Rockstar announced it in September. By November 18, trading volume had reached $5.9 million. Rockstar had released a selection of singles, leaving most of the album’s track list officially unconfirmed.

Contracts on whether the game would earn a review score above 96 drew roughly $80,000, while markets on in-game radio station appearances logged just over $22,000.

The final days before launch also exposed the operational friction of running continuous markets on entertainment releases. On the night of November 13, a video surfaced online purportedly showing the back cover and tracklist of the GTA VI vinyl album.

As a result, the implied probability of Puerto Rican artist Bad Bunny appearing on the album plunged from 49% to 2% on Kalshi.

The Last Contract May Outlast the Launch

With the console release underway, traders are betting on the game's success metrics, including first-week album sales, the timing of a PC port, and the rollout of GTA VI Online.

On Polymarket, traders are pricing a 97% to 98% probability that GTA VI will break the 24-hour entertainment revenue record by surpassing $815.7 million in day-one sales.

The catch is in the rules. The contract counts revenue, and a qualifying figure must be published by January 31, 2027. If none appears in time, the contract settles No even if the record falls.

The release therefore ends only the first and largest GTA VI prediction cycle. As the launch moves across time zones, the market is shifting to how much revenue it will generate and what the publisher releases next.

The years of schedule uncertainty effectively turned Rockstar Games’ release calendar into a liquid hedging and speculation vehicle.

K33 Research said bitcoin is in "deep value territory" after a 14% weekly drop, as ETF outflows, liquidations and hedging demand reach levels seen near past bottoms.

content:
K33 Research said bitcoin is trading in “deep value territory” after a 14% weekly drop, arguing that “any entry below $70K is a gift from the market” for medium- to long-term investors.

The call comes in the firm’s weekly report, “No gain, plenty of pain,” which published Nov. 16. Head of research Vetle Lunde wrote that bitcoin’s slide has erased its August and September gains and left the market deeply oversold. Bitcoin has posted six straight red weekly candles and is on track for a record 13 consecutive days of lower daily highs, according to K33.

Lunde said a streak of six weekly losses has happened only twice before, from Jan. 26 to March 1, 2026, and from April 3 to May 29, 2022. Daily RSI, a momentum gauge, hit 19.95 on Saturday and has stayed below 25 since Friday. Bitcoin also fell below its 200-week moving average, near $68,000, after its worst weekly return since June 7.

Bitcoin below its long-term average

At the bottom on Nov. 15, bitcoin traded about 8.5% under the 200-week average, a wider gap than the 7.3% recorded at June’s low of $58,500. K33 said 51.5% of the bitcoin supply last moved on-chain at prices above the current level, meaning the average holder could have sold for more at some point in the past four years.

Lunde said those readings, taken together, have typically lined up with market bottoms. K33 also noted that crypto has lagged traditional markets, with the Nasdaq and S&P 500 recovering modestly last week while bitcoin sank.

Bitcoin was trading near $62,300 on Wednesday, according to Coinbase spot prices, below the roughly $65,000 level cited in the K33 report, which showed bitcoin down 14% on the week and about 20% over 30 days. Ether also fell 14% over the week, to around $1,827.

Outflows, liquidations and hedging

Capital continues to leave bitcoin funds. Net outflows from bitcoin exchange-traded products reached 44,900 BTC over the 14 trading days since Oct. 29, K33 said, short of the record of about 71,000 BTC set in June. Total ETF holdings fell to about 1.46 million BTC, the lowest since Aug. 19, and leveraged ETF exposure dropped to 21,900 BTC, the lowest since March 2024.

Forced selling hit derivatives, too. About $1.3 billion in long positions were liquidated on Nov. 13 and 14 as bitcoin broke below $70,000, K33 said, and funding rates on perpetual futures repeatedly turned negative. Open interest fell by about 30,000 BTC but stayed above 330,000 BTC, leaving leverage elevated against historical norms.

Institutional futures players largely stayed on the sidelines. Open interest in bitcoin futures on CME stayed below 100,000 BTC all week, K33 said, a sign that regulated-market participants have not rushed in to buy the dip.

Demand for downside protection is also surging. The one-month 25-delta skew, which compares the price of puts to calls, rose above 20 for the first time since July, a level Lunde said has historically coincided with “selling exhaustion near local bottoms.”

Stablecoins offer another sign of stress. K33 said net redemptions totaled $16.1 billion over the past month, the largest outflow since the collapse of Terra.

A bottom, but not a bounce

Lunde stopped short of calling the decline over. He said earlier recoveries from similar conditions involved “prolonged consolidation,” pointing to a choppy recovery rather than an immediate rebound.

There were some constructive signs in trading activity. Spot volume ran near $5 billion a day from Friday through Sunday, the busiest weekend since February, which K33 said could give the market firmer footing after weeks of one-way selling.

Even so, leverage remains high, and ETF money is still heading out the door. Bitcoin was near $62,300 at the time of writing, below the roughly $68,000 200-week average K33 flagged as a key level.
